title: Minimum White Tiles After Covering With Carpets
summary: Given a 0-indexed binary string floor representing the colors of the tiles on a floor, where floor[i] = '0' indicates a black tile and floor[i] = '1' indicates a white tile, and given the number of black carpets (numCarpets) and the length of each carpet (carpetLen), cover the floor with the carpets such that the number of white tiles still visible is minimized.
statement: Given a 0-indexed binary string floor representing the colors of the tiles on a floor, where floor[i] = '0' indicates a black tile and floor[i] = '1' indicates a white tile, and given the number of black carpets (numCarpets) and the length of each carpet (carpetLen), cover the floor with the carpets such that the number of white tiles still visible is minimized. Carpets can overlap. Return the minimum number of white tiles that remain visible.
constraints: floor uses one for white and zero for black tiles.
Each carpet covers carpet_len consecutive positions; carpets may overlap and may extend past the useful suffix.
Use at most num_carpets carpets to minimize uncovered white tiles.
hints: At each leftmost undecided tile, either leave it visible or begin a carpet there.
Memoize by current index and remaining carpets.
Return min(is_white+search(i+1,c), search(i+length,c-1)); handle exhausted floor or carpets.
Every covering has one of these two choices at its first undecided tile, and later cost depends only on the suffix and carpet count.
editorial: Every covering has one of these two choices at its first undecided tile, and later cost depends only on the suffix and carpet count.

tests.explanation: Two length-two carpets can cover all but two white tiles, so return two.
Two carpets can cover the whole length, leaving zero visible white tiles.
